source.title: How Much Regularization Survives Averaging? Update Masking in Federated Learning
source.authors: Wen-Hao Yan; Fu Kuroda; Yu-Cheng Jin; Zhen-Ke Chen

record.tranche_reason: Measures how gradient diversity changes the masking regularization that survives FedAvg, using CIFAR-10 federated measurements rather than the claim versions’ natural-label generalization tests.
record.gate_note: The study reports theoretical curvature-penalty results and measures the recovery factor under local-training and data-heterogeneity conditions. It does not measure random-label memorization, natural-label generalization gaps, or the optimizer, architecture, and explicit-regularization comparisons in the versions.
record.test_reason: The batch-size sweep tests V5 in federated learning: at each fixed local-epoch count, all runs use 200 rounds, the same client-sampling protocol and SGD learning rate, and larger batches yield lower test accuracy. Gradient-diversity measurements themselves do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the conclusion. Independent client masks attenuate the second-order curvature penalty by cohort size; shared masks recover it according to reciprocal gradient diversity under the stated curvature assumptions. The measured Euclidean proxy is near 1.19 in the reference configuration, rises with full-batch training, and is less sensitive to heterogeneity. Higher-recovery configurations have poor accuracy, but the experiments do not establish whether masking improves accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Measures federated update masking and reciprocal gradient diversity in ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10; the claim versions concern natural-label generalization, test error, and generalization-gap predictors.
record.method_sensitivity: Local batch size and local epochs affect recovery factor; full-batch values range from 3.96 to 8.96, while minibatch configurations range from 1.10 to 1.36. Data heterogeneity yields unweighted values from 1.17 to 1.50 across α settings, while uneven shard sizes make weighted and unweighted measures diverge at α = 0.1.

fits_no_version.finding: Reciprocal gradient diversity is much higher with full-batch local training than with minibatches and changes little with heterogeneity under weighted aggregation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this FedAvg setting, minibatch sampling limits the estimated recovery of the update-masking curvature penalty. This proxy does not establish masking's benefit or a sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.

record.problems: Only one architecture and dataset are measured. The paper measures Euclidean rather than Hessian-weighted gradient diversity because the global Hessian is unavailable. Its second-order expansion assumes small updates, which multi-step minibatch training violates; the authors say those near-one recovery measurements are indicative rather than exact. Three seeds are used, with medians reported.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and matched natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning.
Learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization or regularization adaptations; longer-training recovery; language models; the location of a critical batch size.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, train-test gaps and comparisons with alternative generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

missing.what: Batch 128, five local epochs, approximately 20 local steps: test accuracy 0.683 and reciprocal gradient diversity 1.18. This completes the matched five-epoch batch-size comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The fixed budget is 200 federated rounds with matched local epochs and client sampling, not matched optimizer-step counts. The V5 evidence concerns held-out performance at that budget; it does not establish a train-test generalization gap. R5 and R6 have swapped numerical results in the record.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out performance on natural and random labels.
Width sweep and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance.
Large versus small batch held-out performance at fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to train-test gaps.
Effects of removing highly memorized training examples on test accuracy.

relationships.reason: R1–R8 show lower test accuracy with larger batches within every matched local-epoch group; the omitted batch-128, five-epoch cell also follows this ordering (Table I text).
relationships.display_finding: Within each checked group of runs using the same number of local epochs (passes through the local training data), test accuracy decreased as batch size increased. Larger batches also reduced the number of local optimizer updates.

relation.reason: Table I directly compares held-out accuracy across batch sizes under matched local epochs, rounds, learning rate and client-sampling protocol.

tranche.reason: The federated setting supplies a result on V5: larger local batches yield lower test accuracy at each fixed local-epoch count and the same 200-round budget.

source_check.notes: V5 support comes from the test-accuracy comparisons, not reciprocal gradient diversity. Larger batches also reduce local optimizer steps; the study does not isolate a generalization-gap mechanism or empirically establish the benefit of masking.
